ļ»æ# Proposed Rome F16 layer discriminator

## Question and scope

The unresolved cell is the 17-token Rome prompt with F16 KV: candidate/Q2 has top-one 5845 but exact top-five overlap 4/5 against selected full-prompt HF; published-main/Q4 has 5/5. The exact-weight report says the Q4_0 file decodes to bit-identical values for all 196 Q2 matrices. The diagnostic should identify where candidate/Q2 first separates from its lossless-Q4 path, then compare all three paths at that first divergence on identical input arrays. No gate rerun, reference choice, new threshold, or arithmetic-policy change.

## Existing captures and reusable tooling

- `build-low-bits-dev/q2-rome-layer-cut-v1/out/runtime/` retains candidate/Q2's F16/F16 Rome forward: 84 arrays (`layer-<0..27>-<0..2>.f32`), `runtime-input.f32`, and raw `runtime.f32` logits. Instrumented and uninstrumented Q2 logits are byte-identical. Phase 0 is the pre-attention residual input, phase 1 is the post-attention residual, and phase 2 is the post-FFN residual.
- `build-low-bits-dev/q2-rome-layer-cut-v1/out/hf/` retains selected-policy full-prompt HF arrays for the same 84 phases, full logits, head input and rounded head input. HF uses exact decoded Q2 weights, block16 reconstruction at all 196 body Linear inputs and explicit Q6_K head, F32 norms/RoPE/residual/softmax, and F16 K/V storage.
- `build-low-bits-dev/q2-rome-same-input-v1/out/hf/` and `out/same-input-analysis.json` retain 56 independent HF attention/FFN outputs driven by corresponding Q2 stage inputs. At layer 0 phase 0 the Q2/HF input arrays are byte-identical; phase 1 first differs by 3.0935e-5 max / 3.0159e-6 RMS. Crucially, the replay injects saved Q2 phase-0 input for each attention stage and saved Q2 phase-1 input for each FFN stage. At the first Q2-vs-Q4 output divergence, preceding Q2/Q4 phase outputs are still byte-identical, so the existing HF replay is already a third same-input arm. Its 56 outputs cover all candidate first-divergence phases; no new HF run is needed. The script is `q2-rome-same-input-v1/hf-replay.py`.
- `build-low-bits-dev/q2-rome-layer-cut-v1/out/build/native-baseline` and `native-cut` are retained compiled binaries with hashes in `out/execution.json`. `native-cut` is the Qwen3 phase observer from `layer-cut.patch`; it loads a model path at runtime and writes all 84 phase files. `supervise.py` documents the isolated capture and byte-control sequence.
- Fixed full-prompt fixture: `build-low-bits-dev/q2-rome-layer-cut-v1/fixture.json`, prompt index 5, 17 pinned IDs. Existing main/Q4 and candidate/Q2 Rome CLI results are in `q2-q4-lossless-control-v1/evidence/control-out/`.

## Smallest useful run

Capture candidate/Q4 using the already compiled observer; the runtime code stays fixed, so the arm difference against retained candidate/Q2 is weight storage and kernel dispatch.

1. In two fresh output directories, run `/binaries/native-baseline capture /converted/Qwen3-0.6B-lossless-Q4_0.gguf /prepared/fixture.json vulkan:0 /out/runtime` and `/binaries/native-cut capture /converted/Qwen3-0.6B-lossless-Q4_0.gguf /prepared/fixture.json vulkan:0 /out/runtime` as separate processes/containers. Use the same F16 request, F16/F16 KV, Vulkan, direct load, 4 threads, ubatch 512, and Rome17 prompt. The cut writes raw logits and all layer phases. Require baseline/cut full-logit byte identity and a `matrix-paths` witness of exactly `block-int16` before interpreting arrays.
2. Compare new candidate/Q4 phase arrays with retained candidate/Q2 arrays in layer/phase order. Stop at the first bitwise-different phase output. Verify its immediately preceding phase input is byte-identical between Q2/Q4. The existing independent-HF replay for that phase was fed the saved Q2 input, so it is the same input by that equality. Compare the three outputs on this shared 17x1024 input: full-run Q2, full-run Q4, and independent same-input HF. Record exact-value count, max absolute delta, RMS delta, and last-token-row delta for each pair. Do not fit an error bound.
3. The expected smallest informative cut is layer 0 phase 1. Prior Q2/HF layer-0 phase-0 arrays are already byte-identical; confirm Q4 phase 0 matches. The three phase-1 arrays then show layer-0 attention residual results from the same input and F16 KV policy. If a later layer/phase is the first Q2/Q4 output difference, use that phase's preceding shared Q2/Q4 output and the existing HF replay output driven by the matching saved Q2 phase input. Do not treat later full-history HF arrays as same-input when their input hashes differ.
4. Keep Q4 raw logits/top ten as a sanity witness against retained main/Q4 Rome output; six-decimal CLI equality is not a byte-identity claim. Candidate-Q4 and main-Q4 top-ten stdout hashes already match in the exact-weight control.

This localizes a layer phase and distinguishes Q2-versus-Q4 path effects from selected-policy HF at the first shared activation. It does not prove a complete-model cause or amend the original ranking gate.

## Missing inputs and constraints

The converted Q4 GGUF is not present in this workspace; only its report is retained. `q2-q4-lossless-control-v1/evidence/out/Qwen3-0.6B-lossless-Q4_0.gguf.report.json` pins SHA256 `cb2f0a5b36062c7e8a0ca7a212dde8a10a7755f4b6fa2d7ce55171beaa743156`, size 469,081,600 bytes, with all 440,401,920 decoded Q2 values bit checked. The original Q2 GGUF is also not local. Prior rig plans mount it as `/models/Qwen3-0.6B-Q2_0.gguf` and the converted file as `/converted/Qwen3-0.6B-lossless-Q4_0.gguf`. A later run needs that rig artifact or an offline recreation from the pinned Q2 file and converter; no network input is needed.

supported: The Q2 and Q4 candidate runs begin layer 0 with byte-identical phase-0 input, then produce different post-attention residuals.
The first observed difference occurs before cross-layer accumulation: in layer 0 attention/residual work.
At that same Q2 input, candidate Q2 is closer than candidate Q4 to selected-policy HF same-input output (RMS 3.016e-6 vs 5.013e-6; max 3.093e-5 vs 7.486e-5).
The full Q4 observer preserves Q4 logits byte-for-byte against the baseline, and all 84 finite phase arrays were captured.
not_supported: This does not isolate a faulty matmul/kernel: post-attention phase bundles Q/K/V projections, F16 K/V cache rounding, attention reductions, output projection and residual arithmetic.
The Q2 run is not thereby proven correct; HF is a diagnostic reference and differs too.
Later increases in the Q2/Q4 gap, including the large layer-27 FFN output jump, cannot be assigned to one operator because trajectory inputs have already diverged.
The layer-27 trajectory blow-up does not prove a model defect or policy defect by itself; it may amplify tiny early differences in this sensitive prompt.

next_smallest_intervention.recommendation: If the first-layer difference needs causal resolution, capture one layer-0 replay per Q2 and Q4 model from the same pinned phase-0 input, recording Q/K/V projection outputs before cache conversion, exact F16 cache bytes, attention context before O projection, O projection output, and post-attention residual. Compare decoded weights and activation bytes; include an ordered scalar/reference matmul for any first differing projection. Keep HF out of this localization and do not rerun full gates.
decision_rule: First Q/K/V projection mismatch on same input: investigate format-dispatch/decode/matmul kernel.
Q/K/V outputs match but cached half bytes differ: inspect cache conversion/rounding.
Q/K/V and cache bytes match but attention context differs: inspect softmax/reduction order and accumulator behavior.
Attention context matches but O projection/residual differs: inspect output matmul and residual arithmetic.
next_smallest_intervention.why_discriminating: It separates a first-operation discrepancy from F16 cache and attention-reduction effects while holding layer input and decoded model weights fixed.
